title: Minjin Kim
text:
Minjin Kim


I am an Assistant Professor of Second Language Studies, TESOL, and Korean in the Department of Linguistics, Languages, and Cultures at Michigan State University. I serve as Director of the Korean Program and Co-Director of the Second Language Studies Corpus Lab. I earned my Ph.D. in Applied Linguistics from Pennsylvania State University.
My research focuses on corpus linguistics, second language acquisition, and language learning and technology, with a particular interest in generative AI. More broadly, I examine patterns in language produced by second language learners and explore how large-scale language data, computational methods, and AI-assisted technologies can be used to understand and support language teaching, research, and assessment, as well as how AI can be used critically and in research-informed ways in language education.

title: Minjin Kim
text:
Research Areas







Corpus Linguistics


I use corpora, computational methods, and NLP tools to investigate patterns of language use and variation across English, Korean, and other less commonly taught languages. My work spans learner language, academic discourse, and disciplinary communication, with the goal of informing language learning, teaching, and research.









Second Language Acquisition


I investigate how second language learners develop and use language across proficiency levels, time, tasks, and modalities, with attention to developmental patterns, variability, and individual learner trajectories.









AI-Mediated Language Learning & Assessment


I investigate how generative AI, speech technologies, and other computational tools can mediate language learning, feedback, interaction, and assessment.









Critical & Research-Informed AI Use


I explore how AI can be used critically and responsibly in language education, with an emphasis on SLA theory, evidence-based practice, and the evaluation and verification of AI-generated feedback.

title: Research
text:
Second Language Development
I study how complexity, accuracy, fluency, and lexical-syntactic features change over time within and across learners. My work emphasizes longitudinal variability, modality differences, and person-centered patterns of development.

title: Minjin Kim
text: I use learner corpora and other large-scale language data to investigate patterns of language use, variation, and development. I am particularly interested in longitudinal learner data, corpus-informed analysis, and applications of corpus resources to language teaching.

title: Research
text:
AI-Mediated Language Learning and Assessment
A major strand of my current work examines generative AI and speech technologies as mediational tools for language learning and assessment. Rather than treating AI only as a source of automated feedback, I am interested in how it can be designed to provide graduated, contingent support.

title: Research
text:
Korean Language Education
My work in Korean includes learner speech, pronunciation and intonation, AI-supported speaking and assessment, curriculum development, and the creation of language-learning resources for Korean as a foreign language.

title: Minjin Kim
text:
Second Language Acquisition
My work examines how second language learners develop and use language across speaking and writing. I am especially interested in developmental variability, complexity, accuracy, fluency, and the relationship between individual learner trajectories and broader developmental patterns.

title: Minjin Kim
text:
Language Learning & Technology
I investigate how digital technologies can support second language learning, teaching, and research. My work includes corpus tools, speech technologies, AI-mediated learning environments, and computational approaches to language data.

title: Minjin Kim
text:
Generative AI
I explore research-informed uses of generative AI in second language learning and assessment, including AI-mediated dynamic assessment, feedback, interaction, and critical AI literacy. I am particularly interested in how AI can function as a mediational tool rather than simply an answer-generating system.
